quote: Modern mariachi music developed from this ''son'' style, with ''mariachi'' as an alternative name for ''son jalisciense''
they played only string instruments such as guitars and harps and dressed in typical peasant clothing
Most sources agree that the modern mariachi originated in the town of [[Cocula, Jalisco|Cocula]], [[Jalisco]], during the 19th century
founded by [[Gaspar Vargas]] in the late 1890s
a wealthy ''hacienda'' family brought an early mariachi from Cocula to play for President [[Porfirio Díaz]] in 1905
Groups began to wander and play for a fee, which obliged them to incorporate other music into their repertoires, including waltzes and polkas
many farm workers moved to the city, including those from Jalisco, which settled around [[Plaza Garibaldi]]
the popularity of [[jazz]] and [[Cuban music]] introduced the trumpet into mariachi, pushing the violins into a secondary role
the first to sing mariachi was [[Tito Guízar]] in ''[[Allá en el Rancho Grande]]'' in 1936
Fuentes along with Vargas were instrumental in the standardization of much of mariachi music
the first female mariachi performers, [[Lola Beltrán]] and [[Lucha Villa]]
Its use in film also made the music popular and a symbol of ethnic pride for Mexican Americans in the United States.
